tasks.title: Bind reserved lifecycle execution to retained outcomes
tasks.goal: Make an owner-selected lifecycle run journal-ready before scratch, install or handler effects, then retain its per-run truthful outcome for retry/attach.
steps: Freeze an owner-computed command/selected-source plan and choose a pure run ID under the existing lifecycle lease before scratch or prerequisite effects.

Reserve the exact run ID through C.1, durably initialize and reread the matching lifecycle header, mark journal-ready, then permit scratch and tracked lifecycle execution through the incumbent runner.
Build a registered report and per-run outcome marker from actual PhaseOutcome and measured partial evidence; publish/read back report before marker and reply only after validation.
On EOF/crash, inspect the same run ID and marker; recover exact retained bytes or return recovery-required/uncertain without a second handler call. Preserve the legacy default path.
positive_cases: One counted handler effect after ready yields a retained report and marker that replay after response loss or later header replacement.
A parked run retains its identity and does not start a second provider.
negative_cases: A changed command/source snapshot, foreign run ID, or absent journal-ready reaches scratch/install/provider.
A crash after handler effect before marker is reported as no-effects or retried automatically.

tasks.title: Journal direct build and package effects
tasks.goal: Add domain-owned pre-effect identity, partial truth and recovery to direct build/package paths before enabling protected machine submission.
steps: Capture exact build/package plan, before-image/resource ownership and reserved run binding before provider.apply or output directory creation.
Retain completed/partial result and artifact-record link under each existing domain owner; crash after effect but before artifact record remains uncertain, never absent.
Join C.1 reservation under the same domain lease and prove duplicate retry does not invoke build/package providers again.
positive_cases: A lost build/package response attaches to its owner result with the same run ID and no second effect.
Both direct paths expose inspectable partial state after a stopped provider.
negative_cases: A post-effect artifact record substitutes for a pre-effect journal.
An absent record after a counted effect causes a second provider call.

tasks.title: Link deploy journals to reserved operation owners
tasks.goal: Join the incumbent deploy intent/checkpoint/sidecar/receipt chain to C.1 run identity and inspectable recovery without duplicating its transaction engine.
steps: Bind a reserved operation to the exact DeploymentHome and plan hash before effect; require the existing physical locks and admitted target root.
On process exit or crash, report receipt, pending intent, partial publication and unsupported recovery truth from the domain journal; do not infer success from a callback or current bytes alone.
Retain cross-instance/principal refusal and one-writer limits through attach and retry.
positive_cases: A lost deploy response reattaches to the same receipt or pending recovery handle without another apply.
Bound and legacy deploy records retain their original identity and compatibility rules.
negative_cases: A copied receipt/sidecar or same bytes transfer owner identity.
A second client bypasses the deploy lock or runs apply over an unretired intent.

tasks.title: Journal remote publication and reconcile owner lifetime
tasks.goal: Give remote publication its own pre-effect run journal and retained partial result, then prove cross-domain attach/EOF/crash semantics without a daemon.
steps: Bind a prepared exact publication subject/effect plan and remote generation to an owner run journal before repo/tag/release/asset writes; never reuse the registry fact log as this journal.
Reconcile repo-created-before-push, lost atomic push/release response and third-state remote refs without repeating an uncertain effect; retain partial/terminal result for retry.
Review lifecycle, build, package, deploy and publication owners together for API exit, EOF, owner crash, one-writer/parked limits and local attach; unsupported adapters remain unavailable.
Expose read-only typed Build/Package/Deploy retained inspection to the orchestrator without exporting IntentReady as an effect grant; bind host-issued authority and held roots before cold attach.

Before any remote effect, reserve an exact expected 19-upload payload catalogue under C.1, stream and verify a run-scoped local vault while Pending, then publish/read back its complete manifest before Ready; cold attach must not mistake an incomplete vault for effect authority.

Load Mode A approval only from a host-pinned user settings Project at a fixed digest-derived name, validate exact scope/expiry/provenance, and redeem its ID create-new under the owner before any remote effect; a lost redemption response is recovery-required, not permission to retry.

Decompose each remote partition into deterministic individual mutating API calls; write/readback a pending call record immediately before each call, independently reobserve its exact object preconditions, and retain landed/uncertain result before advancing. GitHub multi-object operations are not atomic partition CAS.

For large upload payloads, hold a nofollow single-link vault file through preflight and streaming body delivery with bounded memory, verify exact count/digest and final identity after transfer, and classify any ambiguous POST or stream failure as uncertain without retry.
positive_cases: A lost remote response returns the same run and a retained result or explicit partial/recovery state.
After API exit the owner identity remains inspectable without a permanent service.
negative_cases: A registry Published fact or identical remote bytes is treated as operation completion.
EOF silently restarts publication or an unavailable domain is advertised as callable.
A copied same-path root or a missing/tampered pre-Ready capsule is accepted as Completed or grants a retry effect.
An observed source digest without retained upload bytes, or an interrupted/incomplete vault, is treated as sufficient to delete a prior release or upload a different byte stream.
A caller-provided OwnerControlled assertion, arbitrary approval path, stale approval, or reused approval ID becomes a publication effect grant.
A lost DELETE-release, upload, rename, or finalize response advances to the next API call or replays the uncertain call merely because remote bytes match.
A multi-gigabyte bundle is buffered as one Vec, a streamed upload silently retries after a lost reply, or a changed vault file is treated as an exact sent payload.

The existing xtask dist prepare mutates remote tag/release before the five-target PROP-073 subject exists. An all-assets-ready protected route must capture and validate all target outputs first, then reserve one exact plan before any tag/release/asset/visibility effect. Keep live public Git publication disabled for this 1.1.0 campaign; use only fake hosts and local proof until explicit owner publication instruction.
Prerequisite: accepted M-07-A.1 exact publication subject/effect plan; journal work never authorizes public Git or release.

The expected canonical vault digest is derived from the validated subject before C.1 reservation. Actual byte staging follows reservation while Pending; large ZIPs require bounded streaming rather than preloading all five into memory. No remote effect route is enabled by the vault alone.

Owner-controlled approval is a cooperative same-user filesystem contract across Linux/macOS/Windows, not hostile same-UID protection; local approval and journal readiness still do not authorize a public 1.1.0 Git publication in this campaign.

The first offline call-journal slice may cover tag and release create/replace with fake host only; later slices must cover all 19 uploads/renames, cleanup and finalize before a protected GitHub adapter is callable. Legacy multi-call helpers are not valid owner effects.
